ideal: When a fence names a language and lies in the own text of a unit, checker reads it as a block of that unit.
note: merged the two conditions into one 'when' clause; used 'it' for the fence

ideal: A run exits with code 2 when any of these hold: a frontmatter lists a missing plugin, checker reports that a document has a frontmatter it cannot read, the run asks for a command that is not available, or the run gets code 2 from a plugin.
note: turned the four-way 'at least one' into a flat list after 'any of these'

ideal: When a declared test checks a unit that is not a claim, checker reports a misaiming for it.
note: folded 'project declares the test' into 'a declared test'

ideal: When a unit is miscited, checker reports a misnesting for it.
note: 'it' for the repeated unit

ideal:
A unit is hidden exactly when it is a bug or a conflict, and at least one of these also holds:
- project has a tracker and the unit names no issue
- the unit names an issue that tracker does not know
- the unit names an issue that tracker has closed
- the unit is a bug, project has a runner, and the bug is not tested
- the unit is a conflict that is not paired
note: factored the shared tracker/issue conditions out of both the bug and conflict branches

ideal: A circular frontmatter is a frontmatter checker cannot read.
note: dropped 'the checker' article to match 'checker' usage elsewhere

ideal: A doubled frontmatter is a frontmatter checker cannot read.
note: same pattern as circular frontmatter

ideal: When a test is adrift, checker reports a finding for it.
note: 'it' for the repeated test

ideal: When a fence lies in the own text of a unit, checker reads it as a block of no unit that sits in that unit.
note: 'it'/'that unit' for the repeated fence and unit_1

ideal: When a run gets code 1 from some plugin but code 2 from none, it exits with code 1.
note: 'but...none' for the two plugin conditions

ideal: When a spec cites no axiom and no spec, checker reports a freelancing for it.
note: dropped repeated 'cites' for the second condition

ideal: When a tag names no unit, checker reports a rotting for it.
note: 'it' for the repeated tag

ideal: When project has a tracker and a conflict names no issue, checker reports an untracking for it.
note: 'it' for the repeated conflict

ideal: When a frontmatter is not one with a plugins key, it holds no entry.
note: 'one with a plugins key' avoids repeating 'frontmatter'

ideal: It must be possible to have an axiom, a spec that sits in it, a declared test that carries a tag naming the spec, and a document holding the axiom, the spec and an index, with the index matching the document, while checker reports no finding for anything.
note: chained the six existentials into one running description

ideal: A unit is unfounded exactly when it is one of these: a spec that cites no axiom and no spec, an exception that cites no spec or no fact, or a bug that cites no spec.
note: kept the already-merged exception clause, tightened wording

ideal: When a fence's second word is vocabulary, it has the role of vocabulary.
note: possessive 'fence's second word' instead of 'the second word of the fence'

ideal: When an exception cites a unit that is not a spec or a fact, checker reports a misnesting for it.
note: 'it' for the repeated exception

ideal: A test checks a unit exactly when it carries a tag that names the unit.
note: 'it' for the repeated test

ideal:
A unit is miscited exactly when it is one of these:
- an axiom citing a unit that is not an axiom
- a fact citing a unit
- a spec citing a unit that is not an axiom, a spec or a fact
- an exception citing a unit that is not a spec or a fact
- a bug citing a unit that is not a spec
- a conflict citing a unit
- a term citing a unit
note: switched each bullet to a participle ('citing') for parallelism

ideal: When a claim is tested, checker reports no untesting for it.
note: 'it' for the repeated claim

ideal: When a term cites a unit, checker reports a misnesting for it.
note: 'it' for the repeated term

ideal: When a document starts with a listing frontmatter that does not list a plugin, and the command line of a run does not name the document, checker does not run the plugin over it.
note: folded the frontmatter's two conditions into one relative clause

ideal: When a conflict names an issue that tracker has closed, checker reports an outdated tracking for it.
note: 'it' for the repeated conflict

ideal: When a search that leaves one unit out requires a scenario to happen and leaves out a unit, and the author already asks about leaving some unit out for that scenario, the author also asks about leaving this unit out for it.
note: named the search's own property ('leaves one unit out') inline rather than as a separate bullet

ideal:
A list can be put in a sentence exactly when all of these hold:
- it has three clauses or fewer, and each item is itself one clause
- it has no item with a comma, or it has two clauses or fewer
- it fits a line when put in a sentence
- no clause before its last begins with a time phrase or holds a relative clause
note: merged the two 'no clause before its last' bullets via De Morgan, since neither existing

ideal: When a test is misleading, checker reports a finding for it.
note: 'it' for the repeated test

ideal: When a conflict names an issue that tracker does not know, checker reports a mistracking for it.
note: 'it' for the repeated conflict

ideal: When a run asks for the generate command while a unit's statement is handwritten, checker reports that statement, and the run does not exit with code 0.
note: possessive 'unit's statement', 'that statement' for the repeat

ideal: When project has a tracker and a bug names no issue, checker reports an untracking for it.
note: 'it' for the repeated bug

ideal: When a unit's statement is handwritten, checker does not write that statement when it generates.
note: possessive form, kept 'it' referring to checker as in the source

ideal: When project lists a document among those it checks, and another document that is context for it holds a unit whose formula has no keyword, the analyzer is asked to hold that unit's formula.
note: 'those it checks' and possessive 'unit's formula' tighten the repeats

ideal: When a unit's formula names a word with no reading, or the unit holds more than one formula, its formula cannot be said in words.
note: possessive 'unit's formula', 'its' for the repeat

ideal: When one unit shares a word with another, the analyzer is asked about them together.
note: 'them together' replaces naming both units again

ideal: When a search that leaves one unit out requires a scenario to happen and leaves out a unit, then: the analyzer is asked to hold that unit's formula, the search does not require the unit itself to hold, and the search requires every other unit the analyzer is asked to hold to hold too.
note: rewrote the trailing universal as 'every other unit ... to hold too'

ideal: When the analyzer is asked about one unit together with another, the first is linked to the second through shared words.
note: 'the first'/'the second' instead of repeating unit_1/unit_2

ideal: When a run asks for the check command and checker reports a unit's statement, the run does not exit with code 0.
note: possessive 'a unit's statement'

ideal: When a search that leaves one unit out requires a scenario to happen, that scenario cannot happen while every held unit holds, and the search is asked after the first search is answered.
note: 'that scenario' for the repeat, folded the two conclusions into one sentence

ideal: For every unit, checker writes the unit's statement when it generates exactly when the statement is unwritten or stale.
note: recognised the two implications as one biconditional
